fields.正文: 86 constitute / construct constitute ▷ 朗读 To make up something, count as something, or formally establish it. construct ▷ 朗读 To build something by putting parts together. 逐词对比 手机可左右滑动表格，横向比较用法与例句。 constitute / construct · 用法对照 单词 / 表达 词性、含义与侧重点 常见搭配 / 句型 中英例句 constitute v. 构成；算作；正式建立 说明组成关系，或某行为性质属于什么 constitute a majority; constitute a threat These errors constitute a serious problem. 这些错误构成严重问题。 construct v. 建造；构建 实际建造或有步骤组织抽象内容 construct a bridge; construct an argument They constructed a model of the system. 他们建立了该系统的模型。 核心区别与用法 constitute 主要表示构成、算作或正式建立；construct 表示建造实体，或有步骤地构建理论、模型、论证。前者强调组成关系，后者强调建造过程。 常用搭配与句型 constitute a majority 构成多数；constitute a threat 构成威胁；construct a bridge 建桥；construct an argument 构建论证 易错提醒 A and B constitute C 表示A与B构成C；不是“施工建造C”。constitute 的宾语也可为抽象概念。 Women constitute most of the team. / Engineers constructed a new bridge. 女性占团队成员的大多数。／工程师建了一座新桥。 怎么选？易错点在哪？ A and B constitute C 是组成关系；construct C 是建造过程。constitute a threat 的意思是构成威胁，而不是人为建造一个威胁物体。

fields.例句: The winter was brutal.

fields.英文释义: Causing suffering without caring, or deliberately causing it.

fields.例句: It was a cruel joke.

fields.英文释义: Continuing with great intensity or determination without easing or stopping.
fields.搭配: relentless pressure; relentless pursuit; relentless effort

fields.正文: 87 brutal / cruel / relentless brutal ▷ 朗读 Extremely violent, harsh, or direct. cruel ▷ 朗读 Causing suffering without caring, or deliberately causing it. relentless ▷ 朗读 Continuing with great intensity or determination without easing or stopping. 逐词对比 手机可左右滑动表格，横向比较用法与例句。 brutal / cruel / relentless · 用法对照 单词 / 表达 词性、含义与侧重点 常见搭配 / 句型 中英例句 brutal adj. 残暴的；严酷的 常强调暴力程度或毫不留情 a brutal attack; brutal honesty The winter was brutal. 那个冬天极其严酷。 cruel adj. 残忍的；刻薄的 使人或动物受苦，或不顾他人痛苦 cruel to; a cruel joke It was a cruel joke. 那是个伤人的玩笑。 relentless adj. 持续不减的；毫不松懈的 强调压力、努力或追求持续不止；既可褒义也可贬义，不必含残忍意味 relentless pressure; relentless pursuit; relentless effort They continued their relentless search. 他们继续不懈地搜寻。 relentless 的关键是持续、不松懈，而非残忍；既可说 relentless pressure，也可说 relentless effort。 核心区别与用法 cruel 强调造成痛苦或对痛苦无动于衷，可涉及肉体或情感；brutal 常强调暴力、野蛮、毫不留情，也可形容极其严酷的条件。 常用搭配与句型 be cruel to animals 虐待动物；a cruel remark 伤人的话；a brutal attack 残暴的袭击；brutally honest 直率得不留情面 易错提醒 正确拼写是 cruel，不是 crul。brutally honest 不一定指暴力，而是说话很直接、可能令人难受。 It was cruel to mock him. / She gave a brutally honest answer. 嘲笑他很残忍。／她给了一个直率得毫不留情的回答。 怎么选？易错点在哪？ brutal 强调残暴、强烈或严酷；cruel 强调造成痛苦或不顾他人痛苦；relentless 强调持续、不放松。a brutal attack 是残暴袭击，a cruel joke 是伤人的玩笑，relentless effort 是不懈努力。relentless 可赞扬坚持，不能一概译为“残忍”；relentless attacks 则可带负面意义。 和第36组相比，persistent 强调持续或反复，tenacious 强调紧抓不放，relentless 更强调强度不减。ruthless 偏为达目的不顾他人，merciless 偏不留情，harsh 偏严厉或刺耳；这些也不是严格的强弱等级。

fields.搭配: obligated to do; feel obligated
fields.例句: I felt obligated to reply.

fields.正文: 88 obliged / obligated obliged ▷ 朗读 Required to do something; also grateful for a favor. obligated ▷ 朗读 Bound by a duty, promise, or rule to do something. 逐词对比 手机可左右滑动表格，横向比较用法与例句。 obliged / obligated · 用法对照 单词 / 表达 词性、含义与侧重点 常见搭配 / 句型 中英例句 obliged adj./过去分词：有义务的；感激的 义务义与 obligated 重叠，另有感谢义 obliged to do; much obliged I'm much obliged for your help. 非常感谢你的帮助。 obligated adj./过去分词：有义务的 常见于美式英语，强调承担责任或义务 obligated to do; feel obligated I felt obligated to reply. 我觉得有义务回复。 核心区别与用法 在“有义务、被迫”义上，两者常可互换；obliged 在英式英语中很常见，obligated 在美式英语中常见，不能硬分成礼貌义务与法律义务。obliged 另有感激义。 常用搭配与句型 be obliged/obligated to do 有义务做；feel obliged to do 感到不得不做；much obliged 非常感谢；oblige someone by doing 做某事以帮忙 易错提醒 I am much obliged 表达感谢；通常不用 much obligated 替代。be obliged to do 也可源于现实压力。 We are obliged to follow the rules. / Much obliged for your help. 我们有义务遵守规则。／非常感谢你的帮助。 怎么选？易错点在哪？ 义务义两者大多可互换，不要硬分成道德义务与法律义务。much obliged 是表达感谢的固定用法，一般不用 much obligated 替换。

fields.英文释义: A serious agreement between people, groups, or countries.
fields.搭配: make a pact; a peace pact
fields.例句: We made a pact to keep in touch.

fields.英文释义: A binding agreement; as a verb, to make an agreement, become smaller, or catch an illness.
fields.搭配: sign a contract; a contract with
fields.例句: They signed a two-year contract.
fields.例句译文: 他们签了一份两年期合同。

fields.英文释义: A shared decision, arrangement, or state of having the same opinion.
fields.搭配: reach an agreement; be in agreement
fields.例句: We finally reached an agreement.

fields.正文: 89 pact / contract / agreement pact ▷ 朗读 A serious agreement between people, groups, or countries. contract ▷ 朗读 A binding agreement; as a verb, to make an agreement, become smaller, or catch an illness. agreement ▷ 朗读 A shared decision, arrangement, or state of having the same opinion. 逐词对比 手机可左右滑动表格，横向比较用法与例句。 pact / contract / agreement · 用法对照 单词 / 表达 词性、含义与侧重点 常见搭配 / 句型 中英例句 pact n. 协定；约定 常为较郑重承诺，可涉及国家也可涉及个人 make a pact; a peace pact We made a pact to keep in touch. 我们约定保持联系。 contract n./v. 合同；订约 常明确双方权利义务，也有其他动词义 sign a contract; a contract with They signed a two-year contract. 他们签了一份两年期合同。 agreement n. 协议；意见一致 最宽泛，可指正式协议或单纯达成共识 reach an agreement; be in agreement We finally reached an agreement. 我们终于达成一致。 核心区别与用法 agreement 是协议或意见一致的总称；pact 常指个人、团体或国家间较郑重的约定；contract 常指包含权利义务的合同。日常理解合同即可，法律效力不能只凭词判断。 常用搭配与句型 make a pact 立约；a peace pact 和平协定；sign a contract 签合同；reach an agreement 达成协议 易错提醒 pact 不一定涉及国家，也可指朋友间的承诺。agreement 可以指书面协议，也可以只是意见一致。 They made a pact to keep in touch. / She signed an employment contract. 他们约定保持联系。／她签了一份劳动合同。 怎么选？易错点在哪？ agreement 最宽泛，pact 常显得郑重，contract 常是明确权利义务的合同。是否有法律约束力不能仅靠词名判断，这里比较的是常见英语用法。

fields.释义: n. 工作团队；机组；船员
fields.英文释义: A team working together, especially on a ship, aircraft, or production.
fields.搭配: a crew member; a film crew
fields.例句: The film crew arrived early.

fields.英文释义: The people employed by an organization; to provide workers for it.
fields.搭配: a staff member; office staff
fields.例句: Ask a member of staff for help.

fields.英文释义: Things or material in general; to fill something tightly.
fields.搭配: a lot of stuff; stuff A into B
fields.例句: Don't leave your stuff here.
fields.例句译文: 别把你的东西留在这里。

fields.正文: 90 crew / staff / stuff crew ▷ 朗读 A team working together, especially on a ship, aircraft, or production. staff ▷ 朗读 The people employed by an organization; to provide workers for it. stuff ▷ 朗读 Things or material in general; to fill something tightly. 逐词对比 手机可左右滑动表格，横向比较用法与例句。 crew / staff / stuff · 用法对照 单词 / 表达 词性、含义与侧重点 常见搭配 / 句型 中英例句 crew n. 工作团队；机组；船员 共同操作交通工具或完成特定工作的一组人 a crew member; a film crew The film crew arrived early. 摄制组很早就到了。 staff n. 员工总称 机构或企业的员工团队，不限于同一具体任务 a staff member; office staff Ask a member of staff for help. 向一名工作人员求助。 stuff n./v. 东西；塞满 名词通常不可数且较口语；与员工无关 a lot of stuff; stuff A into B Don't leave your stuff here. 别把你的东西留在这里。 核心区别与用法 crew 是共同操作船、飞机或完成特定工作的团队；staff 是机构的员工总称；stuff 通常是不可数的“东西、材料、事情”。staff 与 stuff 只是拼写相近。 常用搭配与句型 a cabin crew 客舱乘务组；a film crew 摄制组；a staff member 一名员工；personal stuff 私人物品 易错提醒 一名机组人员说 a crew member，一名员工说 a staff member；“很多东西”说 a lot of stuff，不说 many stuffs。 The crew prepared for take-off. / Leave your stuff here. 机组人员准备起飞。／把你的东西放在这里。 怎么选？易错点在哪？ crew 看共同执行的专门工作；staff 看机构员工身份；stuff 是东西。说 a crew member / a staff member；stuff 通常不可数，不说 many stuffs。

fields.英文释义: To cause action or give a cue; quick to act; a cue or instruction.
fields.搭配: prompt sb to do; a prompt response
fields.例句: The news prompted a debate.

fields.英文释义: To strongly encourage action; a strong desire to do something.
fields.搭配: urge sb to do; an urge to do
fields.例句: They urged me to apply.

fields.英文释义: To give confidence or support, or make something more likely.
fields.搭配: encourage sb to do; encourage growth
fields.例句: She encouraged me to keep trying.

fields.正文: 91 prompt / urge / encourage prompt ▷ 朗读 To cause action or give a cue; quick to act; a cue or instruction. urge ▷ 朗读 To strongly encourage action; a strong desire to do something. encourage ▷ 朗读 To give confidence or support, or make something more likely. 逐词对比 手机可左右滑动表格，横向比较用法与例句。 prompt / urge / encourage · 用法对照 单词 / 表达 词性、含义与侧重点 常见搭配 / 句型 中英例句 prompt v./adj./n. 促使；及时的；提示 可引发行动或反应，也指及时回应与提示内容 prompt sb to do; a prompt response The news prompted a debate. 这则消息引发了讨论。 urge v./n. 敦促；强烈冲动 劝说力度强，常带急迫感 urge sb to do; an urge to do They urged me to apply. 他们力劝我申请。 encourage v. 鼓励；促进 给予支持和信心，或使某行为更可能发生 encourage sb to do; encourage growth She encouraged me to keep trying. 她鼓励我继续尝试。 核心区别与用法 prompt 作动词表示促使某人行动或引发反应；urge 强调强烈敦促；encourage 强调给予鼓励或支持。prompt 另可作形容词“及时的”和名词“提示”。 常用搭配与句型 prompt sb to do 促使某人做；urge sb to do 敦促某人做；encourage sb to do 鼓励某人做；a prompt reply 及时回复；a writing prompt 写作提示 易错提醒 prompt 不只是AI“提示词”。The news prompted a debate 中意为消息引发了讨论；urge 的语气通常更急迫。 The question prompted me to think. / My teacher encouraged me to try again. 这个问题促使我思考。／老师鼓励我再试一次。 怎么选？易错点在哪？ 引发行动用 prompt；强烈劝说用 urge；给予信心支持用 encourage。prompt 的及时义、提示义都很常见，不只用于AI提示词。

fields.英文释义: To take something temporarily with the intention of returning it.
fields.搭配: borrow sth from sb
fields.例句: I borrowed a book from Tom.

fields.英文释义: To let someone use something temporarily with the expectation of its return.
fields.搭配: lend sth to sb; lend sb sth
fields.例句: Tom lent me a book.

fields.正文: 92 borrow / lend borrow ▷ 朗读 To take something temporarily with the intention of returning it. lend ▷ 朗读 To let someone use something temporarily with the expectation of its return. 逐词对比 手机可左右滑动表格，横向比较用法与例句。 borrow / lend · 用法对照 单词 / 表达 词性、含义与侧重点 常见搭配 / 句型 中英例句 borrow v. 借入 主语暂时拿来别人的东西 borrow sth from sb I borrowed a book from Tom. 我向汤姆借了一本书。 lend v. 借出 主语把东西暂时交给别人；过去式 lent lend sth to sb; lend sb sth Tom lent me a book. 汤姆借给我一本书。 核心区别与用法 borrow 从别人那里借入；lend 把自己的东西借给别人。二者描述同一借用关系的不同方向。borrowed 为规则过去式，lend 的过去式与过去分词为 lent。 常用搭配与句型 borrow sth from sb 向某人借入；lend sth to sb / lend sb sth 借给某人；a library loan 图书借阅 易错提醒 不要说 borrow me a pen；应说 lend me a pen。表达借了多久常用 keep：May I keep it for a week? borrow 常强调借入动作。 Can I borrow your pen? / Could you lend me your pen? 我能借你的笔吗？／你能把笔借给我吗？ 怎么选？易错点在哪？ 借入用 borrow，借出用 lend。lend 的过去式是 lent；表达“保留借来的物品多久”常用 keep，例如 Can I keep it for a week?

fields.英文释义: To use money, time, or effort on something.
fields.搭配: spend on; spend time doing
fields.例句: I spent an hour reading.

fields.英文释义: To require money, time, or sacrifice; the amount required.
fields.搭配: sth costs sb money; cost of
fields.例句: The book cost me £10.

fields.英文释义: In time expressions, to require a particular amount of time.
fields.搭配: It takes sb time to do
fields.例句: It took me an hour to finish.

fields.英文释义: To give money for something or settle a debt; wages.
fields.搭配: pay for sth; pay sb money
fields.例句: I paid £10 for the book.

fields.正文: 93 spend / cost / take / pay spend ▷ 朗读 To use money, time, or effort on something. cost ▷ 朗读 To require money, time, or sacrifice; the amount required. take ▷ 朗读 In time expressions, to require a particular amount of time. pay ▷ 朗读 To give money for something or settle a debt; wages. 逐词对比 手机可左右滑动表格，横向比较用法与例句。 spend / cost / take / pay · 用法对照 单词 / 表达 词性、含义与侧重点 常见搭配 / 句型 中英例句 spend v. 花费 以人或组织为主语，花钱或花时间 spend on; spend time doing I spent an hour reading. 我花了一小时阅读。 cost v./n. 花费；代价 以物品或事情为主语，表示使人付出钱或代价 sth costs sb money; cost of The book cost me £10. 这本书花了我10英镑。 take v. 需要；花费 说明活动所需时间，常用形式主语 it It takes sb time to do It took me an hour to finish. 我花了一小时完成。 pay v./n. 支付；工资 强调付钱的动作；也可表示付出代价 pay for sth; pay sb money I paid £10 for the book. 我付了10英镑买这本书。 核心区别与用法 spend 以花费者为主语，花时间或钱；cost 常以物品或行为为主语说明代价；take 常说明某事需要多久；pay 强调付款。 常用搭配与句型 spend time/money on sth；spend time doing；sth costs sb money；It takes sb time to do；pay for sth；pay sb money 易错提醒 常见错误是 spend time to do，通常应改为 spend time doing。cost 不只指钱：It cost him his job 表示使他失去工作。 I spent two hours reading. / The book cost me £10. / I paid £10 for it. 我花了两小时阅读。／这本书花了我10英镑。／我为它付了10英镑。 怎么选？易错点在哪？ 人 spend 时间 doing，物 cost 人多少钱，It takes 人 时间 to do，人 pay 钱 for 物。不要把 spend time doing 写成 spend time to do。

fields.英文释义: To keep something in your memory or bring it back to mind.
fields.搭配: remember to do; remember doing
fields.例句: Remember to close the window.

fields.英文释义: To make someone remember or think of something.
fields.搭配: remind sb to do; remind sb of
fields.例句: Remind me to call her.

fields.英文释义: To bring something back to mind; also to officially request its return.
fields.搭配: recall doing; recall a product
fields.例句: I recall meeting her before.

fields.正文: 94 remember / remind / recall remember ▷ 朗读 To keep something in your memory or bring it back to mind. remind ▷ 朗读 To make someone remember or think of something. recall ▷ 朗读 To bring something back to mind; also to officially request its return. 逐词对比 手机可左右滑动表格，横向比较用法与例句。 remember / remind / recall · 用法对照 单词 / 表达 词性、含义与侧重点 常见搭配 / 句型 中英例句 remember v. 记得；想起 记住未来任务或回想过去经历 remember to do; remember doing Remember to close the window. 记得关窗。 remind v. 提醒；使想起 让另一个人想起；通常需要人的宾语 remind sb to do; remind sb of Remind me to call her. 提醒我给她打电话。 recall v./n. 回忆；召回 回想过去，较正式；也可召回产品 recall doing; recall a product I recall meeting her before. 我记得以前见过她。 核心区别与用法 remember 表示自己记得或想起；remind 表示使别人想起或提醒；recall 表示回想，语气通常较正式，也可指召回产品。 常用搭配与句型 remember to do 记得要做；remember doing 记得做过；remind sb of sth 使某人想起；remind sb to do 提醒某人做；recall doing 回想起做过 易错提醒 remember to lock 是记得去锁；remember locking 是记得已经锁过。remind 通常需要宾语，不能直接说 remind to do。 Remember to call her. / This song reminds me of home. / I recall meeting him. 记得给她打电话。／这首歌使我想起家。／我记得见过他。 怎么选？易错点在哪？ remember to do 是记得要做；remember doing 是记得做过。remind 是让别人记起，常要接人的宾语；recall doing 适用于回想过去经历。

fields.英文释义: To adjust to new conditions or change something for a new use.
fields.搭配: adapt to; adapt A for B
fields.例句: It takes time to adapt to change.

fields.英文释义: To begin using an idea or method, or legally take a child into your family.
fields.搭配: adopt a method; adopt a child
fields.例句: We adopted a new approach.

fields.正文: 95 adapt / adopt adapt ▷ 朗读 To adjust to new conditions or change something for a new use. adopt ▷ 朗读 To begin using an idea or method, or legally take a child into your family. 逐词对比 手机可左右滑动表格，横向比较用法与例句。 adapt / adopt · 用法对照 单词 / 表达 词性、含义与侧重点 常见搭配 / 句型 中英例句 adapt v. 适应；改编；调整 改变自身或事物以适合新环境、用途 adapt to; adapt A for B It takes time to adapt to change. 适应变化需要时间。 adopt v. 采用；收养 接受方法、政策或态度，也可收养孩子 adopt a method; adopt a child We adopted a new approach. 我们采用了新方法。 核心区别与用法 adapt 表示适应新条件，或改编、调整已有事物；adopt 表示采用方法、政策或态度，也可表示收养。两词只差一个字母但意思不同。 常用搭配与句型 adapt to a new environment 适应新环境；adapt a novel for film 把小说改编成电影；adopt a policy 采用政策；adopt a child 收养孩子 易错提醒 adapt to 中 to 是介词，后接名词或动名词；adopt 后通常直接接政策、方法等宾语。 Students adapt to university life. / The school adopted a new policy. 学生适应大学生活。／学校采用了一项新政策。 怎么选？易错点在哪？ adapt 调整以适应；adopt 接受采用或收养。adapt to 的 to 为介词，后接名词或动名词；adopt a method 中不需要 to。

fields.英文释义: Relating to the economy or the study of economics.
fields.搭配: economic growth; economic policy
fields.例句: The country faces economic problems.
fields.例句译文: 这个国家面临经济问题。

fields.释义: adj. 节约的；经济实惠的
fields.英文释义: Using money, fuel, or other resources carefully and without waste.
fields.搭配: economical to run; economical with
fields.例句: This car is economical to run.

fields.正文: 96 economic / economical economic ▷ 朗读 Relating to the economy or the study of economics. economical ▷ 朗读 Using money, fuel, or other resources carefully and without waste. 逐词对比 手机可左右滑动表格，横向比较用法与例句。 economic / economical · 用法对照 单词 / 表达 词性、含义与侧重点 常见搭配 / 句型 中英例句 economic adj. 经济的；经济学的 常说明与经济活动有关，而非一定省钱 economic growth; economic policy The country faces economic problems. 这个国家面临经济问题。 economical adj. 节约的；经济实惠的 强调使用金钱、燃料、时间等较节省 economical to run; economical with This car is economical to run. 这辆车使用成本低。 核心区别与用法 economic 表示与经济、经济学有关的；economical 表示节约钱、燃料、时间等，突出资源使用效率。economic 在某些语境中也可有“合算的”意思。 常用搭配与句型 economic growth 经济增长；economic policy 经济政策；an economical car 省油且使用经济的车；economical with resources 节约资源 易错提醒 “经济发展”用 economic development；形容设备省钱常用 economical，不要仅凭中文都有“经济”就互换。 Economic growth slowed. / This heater is economical to run. 经济增长放缓了。／这台取暖器运行成本低。 怎么选？易错点在哪？ 经济政策用 economic，节省运行成本用 economical。economic 在部分语境也有合算义，所以不是所有省钱表达都只能用 economical；先记常见搭配。

fields.英文释义: To make certain that something happens or is true.
fields.搭配: ensure that; ensure safety
fields.例句: Check the lock to ensure safety.

fields.英文释义: To tell someone confidently that something is true so they feel less worried.
fields.搭配: assure sb that; assure sb of
fields.例句: I assured him that I would help.

fields.英文释义: To arrange or provide financial protection against specified risks.
fields.搭配: insure against; insure a car
fields.例句: The house is insured against fire.

fields.正文: 97 ensure / assure / insure ensure ▷ 朗读 To make certain that something happens or is true. assure ▷ 朗读 To tell someone confidently that something is true so they feel less worried. insure ▷ 朗读 To arrange or provide financial protection against specified risks. 逐词对比 手机可左右滑动表格，横向比较用法与例句。 ensure / assure / insure · 用法对照 单词 / 表达 词性、含义与侧重点 常见搭配 / 句型 中英例句 ensure v. 确保 采取行动使结果可靠地发生 ensure that; ensure safety Check the lock to ensure safety. 检查锁以确保安全。 assure v. 向……保证；使放心 常对某人作保证，直接宾语通常是人 assure sb that; assure sb of I assured him that I would help. 我向他保证我会帮忙。 insure v. 投保；承保 常用于保险，也有确保义，尤其美式用法 insure against; insure a car The house is insured against fire. 这所房子投保了火险。 核心区别与用法 ensure 强调确保某事发生；assure 强调向某人保证、使其放心；insure 常指为风险投保。在美式用法中 insure 有时也用于确保，但区分记忆更清晰。 常用搭配与句型 ensure safety 确保安全；ensure that… 确保……；assure sb that… 向某人保证……；insure a car 给汽车投保；insure against loss 投保防损失 易错提醒 assure 的常见直接宾语是人；不要把 ensure someone that 当作 assure someone that 使用。assure 本身也有保险领域用法，需看具体语境。 Please ensure that the door is locked. / I assured her that everything was ready. 请确保门已锁好。／我向她保证一切准备好了。 怎么选？易错点在哪？ 确保结果常用 ensure；让人放心常用 assure sb；投保常用 insure。美式 insure 有时也能表示确保，但不要据此把所有句型互换。

fields.正文: 98 efficient / effective efficient ▷ 朗读 Achieving a result with little wasted time, energy, or resources. effective ▷ 朗读 Producing the intended result; also officially in force. 逐词对比 手机可左右滑动表格，横向比较用法与例句。 efficient / effective · 用法对照 单词 / 表达 词性、含义与侧重点 常见搭配 / 句型 中英例句 efficient adj. 高效的 用较少的资源、时间或精力完成工作 an efficient system; energy-efficient The new system is more efficient. 新系统效率更高。 effective adj. 有效的；生效的 达到预期效果，或正式开始适用 an effective method; effective from The method is effective but slow. 方法有效，但速度慢。 核心区别与用法 efficient 强调以较少的时间、精力或资源完成任务；effective 强调确实产生预期效果。一个方法可以有效但费时，也可以流程很高效却解决错了问题。 常用搭配与句型 an efficient worker 高效的员工；energy-efficient 节能的；an effective method 有效的方法；be effective in doing 在做某事方面有效 易错提醒 评价节约资源时考虑 efficient；评价是否实现目的时考虑 effective。不能把两者固定解释为“速度快”和“效果强”。 The method is effective but not very efficient: it works, yet takes too long. 这种方法有效但效率不高：它能奏效，却耗时过长。 怎么选？易错点在哪？ efficient 看资源利用，effective 看是否奏效。方法可以有效但低效，也可能执行高效却未实现目标；两词关注不同评价维度。

fields.正文: 99 accept / receive accept ▷ 朗读 To willingly take, agree to, or recognize something. receive ▷ 朗读 To get something that is sent, given, or provided. 逐词对比 手机可左右滑动表格，横向比较用法与例句。 accept / receive · 用法对照 单词 / 表达 词性、含义与侧重点 常见搭配 / 句型 中英例句 accept v. 接受；认可 态度上同意接纳，不只是到手 accept an offer; accept responsibility She accepted the invitation. 她接受了邀请。 receive v. 收到；得到 东西、信息、待遇等到达，不必表示同意 receive an email; receive support She received the invitation yesterday. 她昨天收到了邀请。 核心区别与用法 receive 表示收到、接到，强调东西或信息到达；accept 表示接受、同意接纳，强调态度或决定。收到邀请不意味着接受邀请。 常用搭配与句型 receive an email 收到邮件；receive an invitation 收到邀请；accept an offer 接受提议；accept responsibility 承担责任 易错提醒 receive 可用于待遇或经历：receive support 得到支持。accept 也可表示承认事实，不只接收实体。 I received the invitation but did not accept it. 我收到了邀请，但没有接受。 怎么选？易错点在哪？ 收到邀请用 receive，决定应邀用 accept。receive 不表示一定自愿接受；accept responsibility 又是承担责任，不能简单译为收到责任。

fields.正文: 100 likely / possible / probable likely ▷ 朗读 Expected to happen or probably true. possible ▷ 朗读 Able to happen or be done, without saying it is likely. probable ▷ 朗读 Likely to happen or be true. 逐词对比 手机可左右滑动表格，横向比较用法与例句。 likely / possible / probable · 用法对照 单词 / 表达 词性、含义与侧重点 常见搭配 / 句型 中英例句 likely adj./adv. 很可能的；很可能 常用于预测人或事物会怎样 be likely to do; It is likely that She is likely to win. 她很可能获胜。 possible adj. 可能的 未被排除，未必概率很大 It is possible that; possible for sb to do It is possible that he forgot. 他有可能忘了。 probable adj. 很可能的 比仅仅 possible 更倾向会发生，较正式 It is probable that; a probable cause Rain is the probable cause of the delay. 雨很可能是延误的原因。 核心区别与用法 possible 表示有可能；probable 表示很可能；likely 也表示可能性较大，且常用于某人或某物预计会怎样。具体概率不能机械换算成百分比。 常用搭配与句型 It is possible for sb to do；It is probable/likely that…；sb is likely to do；a likely outcome 可能出现的结果 易错提醒 表达“他可能来”用 He is likely to come 或 It is possible that he will come，不用 He is possible to come。likely 在部分用法中也可作副词。 She is likely to pass. / It is possible that the train will be late. 她很可能通过。／火车有可能晚点。 怎么选？易错点在哪？ possible 只说有可能，likely/probable 通常倾向很可能，但不能固定成百分比。说 He is likely to come；不说 He is possible/probable to come。

fields.正文: 101 organized / organizational organized ▷ 朗读 Able to plan things neatly and effectively; also arranged in a structured way. organizational ▷ 朗读 Relating to how an organization or activity is structured, managed, or coordinated. 逐词对比 手机可左右滑动表格，横向比较用法与例句。 organized / organizational · 用法对照 单词 / 表达 词性、含义与侧重点 常见搭配 / 句型 中英例句 organized adj. 有条理的；有组织的 形容人做事有条理，或活动经过安排；也可作 organize 的过去式/过去分词 an organized person; well-organized notes She is organized and always meets deadlines. 她做事有条理，总能按时完成任务。 organizational adj. 组织的；组织管理方面的 说明与组织结构、管理或协调能力有关，不直接表示一个人有条理 organizational skills; organizational structure The job requires strong organizational skills. 这份工作要求很强的组织协调能力。 怎么选？易错点在哪？ 形容“你很有条理”用 You are organized；说“组织协调能力”用 organizational skills。organized 是对状态或特点的评价，organizational 是“与组织管理有关”的关系形容词。organized activities 是有组织的活动；organizational changes 是组织层面的变动。

fields.正文: 102 assign / arrange assign ▷ 朗读 To give someone a task or role, or designate something for a particular use. arrange ▷ 朗读 To plan something or put things in a particular order. 逐词对比 手机可左右滑动表格，横向比较用法与例句。 assign / arrange · 用法对照 单词 / 表达 词性、含义与侧重点 常见搭配 / 句型 中英例句 assign v. 分配；指派；指定 把具体任务、角色或资源交给某人，也可给事物赋值或归类 assign sb a task; assign a task to sb; assign sb to a team The teacher assigned each student a topic. 老师给每名学生分配了一个题目。 arrange v. 安排；筹备；整理 协调时间、活动或摆放顺序，重点不在把任务交给谁 arrange a meeting; arrange for sb to do; arrange to do We arranged for a taxi to pick her up. 我们安排了一辆出租车去接她。 怎么选？易错点在哪？ assign 回答“把什么交给谁”，arrange 回答“怎么安排好”。可以先 assign tasks to team members，再 arrange a meeting。安排某人做事常用 arrange for sb to do，不能机械套成 arrange sb to do。原网站的 appoint / arrange 仍保留，appoint 侧重正式任命。

fields.正文: 103 property / asset property ▷ 朗读 Something owned, especially land or buildings; also a characteristic of a thing. asset ▷ 朗读 Something valuable or useful, especially a resource with economic value. 逐词对比 手机可左右滑动表格，横向比较用法与例句。 property / asset · 用法对照 单词 / 表达 词性、含义与侧重点 常见搭配 / 句型 中英例句 property n. 财产；房产；性质 所有物的总称；也指房地产或事物的特性，强调归属或性质 private property; a property owner; physical properties This land is private property. 这块土地是私人财产。 asset n. 资产；有价值的人或事物 强调具有经济价值、能带来益处；可包括现金、专利、技能等 financial assets; a valuable asset; an asset to the team Her language skills are an asset to the team. 她的语言能力是团队的一大优势。 怎么选？易错点在哪？ 同一栋房子可以是你的 property，也可以是你的 asset：前者强调所有权或房产类别，后者强调经济价值。property 作财产总称通常不可数，但 a property 可指一处房产；properties 也可指性质。asset 可数，常用复数 assets；名词 property 没有“团队优势”这个常见用法。

fields.正文: 106 strain strain ▷ 朗读 Pressure or excessive effort; an injury from overstretching; a biological variety; to exert effort or filter liquid. 逐词对比 手机可左右滑动表格，横向比较用法与例句。 strain · 用法对照 单词 / 表达 词性、含义与侧重点 常见搭配 / 句型 中英例句 strain n./v. 压力；拉伤；品系；用力；过滤 多义词：精神或身体的负担、肌肉拉伤、生物品系；动词可指使劲或滤去液体中的固体 under strain; a muscle strain; a strain of virus; strain to hear; strain the sauce She strained to hear the quiet voice. 她竭力想听清那个轻轻的声音。 怎么选？易错点在哪？ strain 不能只记为“拉伤”：under strain 表示承受压力，a muscle strain 是肌肉或肌腱拉伤，a strain of bacteria 是细菌菌株。strain to do 表示费力做，strain one's eyes 是过度用眼，strain the soup 是过滤汤。sprain 通常指韧带扭伤；不要把它与 strain 的损伤义混为一谈。

fields.搭配: 动词变化为 stroke–stroked–stroked。a stroke of luck 是一次好运；a stroke of genius 是神来之笔；at a stroke 是一下子。heatstroke（也写作 heat stroke）指中暑，不能与脑卒中混淆。

fields.搭配: 动词变化为 stroke–stroked–stroked。a stroke of luck 是一次好运；a stroke of genius 是神来之笔；at a stroke 是一下子。heatstroke（也写作 heat stroke）指中暑，不能与脑卒中混淆。

fields.例句译文: 演出在午夜钟声敲响时开始。

records.title: Take Naps at Work. Apologize to No One [A]

fields.原文: In the past two weeks I've taken three naps at work, a total of an hour or so of shut-eye while on the clock. And I have no shame or uncertainty about doing it. I couldn't feel better about it, and my productivity reflects it, too.
fields.译文: 过去两周，我在工作时睡了三次午觉，在上班时间合计睡了大约一个小时。我对此既不羞愧，也没有犹豫。我感觉好极了，工作效率也体现了这一点。

records.title: Take Naps at Work. Apologize to No One [B]

fields.原文: Sleeping on the job is one of those workplace taboos—like leaving your desk for lunch or taking an afternoon walk—that we're taught to look down on. If someone naps at 2 p.m. while the rest of us furiously write memos and respond to emails, surely it must mean they're slacking off. Or so the assumption goes.
fields.译文: 上班时睡觉是职场禁忌之一，就像离开办公桌去吃午饭或下午出去散步一样，我们从小被教导要对此抱有负面看法。如果有人下午两点在打盹，而我们其他人正忙着写备忘录、回复邮件，那一定说明他在偷懒。至少人们通常这样认为。

records.title: Take Naps at Work. Apologize to No One [C]

fields.原文: Restfulness and recharging can take a back seat to the perception and appearance of productivity. It's easier to stay on a virtual hamster wheel of activity by immediately responding to every email than it is to measure aggregate productivity over a greater period of time. But a growing field of occupational and psychological research is building the case for restfulness in pursuit of greater productivity.
fields.译文: 休息和恢复精力，往往让位于看起来很有效率、表现得很忙碌。立即回复每封邮件，让自己像仓鼠一样在虚拟的跑轮上不停忙碌，比衡量较长一段时间内的整体工作效率更容易。但越来越多的职业与心理学研究正在证明，为了提高工作效率，人们需要充分休息。

records.title: Take Naps at Work. Apologize to No One [D]

fields.原文: Companies are suffering from tremendous productivity problems because people are stressed out and not recovering from the workday, said Josh Bersin, Principal and Founder of Bersin by Deloitte. “They're beginning to realize that this is their problem, and they can't just say to people, ‘Here's a work-life balance course, go teach yourself how to manage your inbox,’” Mr. Bersin said. “It's way more complicated than that.”
fields.译文: 德勤旗下贝尔森研究机构的创始人兼负责人乔希·贝尔森说，由于员工压力过大，而且无法从一天的工作中恢复过来，公司正面临严重的效率问题。他说：“他们开始意识到，这是公司自身的问题，不能只对员工说：‘这里有一门工作与生活平衡的课程，自己去学怎么管理收件箱吧。’实际情况要复杂得多。”

records.title: Take Naps at Work. Apologize to No One [E]

fields.原文: To be sure, the ability to nap at work is far from widespread, experts said. Few among us have the luxury of being able to step away for a half-hour snoozefest. But lunch hours and coffee breaks can be great times to duck out, and your increased productivity and alertness will be all the evidence you need to make your case to inquiring bosses.
fields.译文: 专家表示，当然，能在工作时午睡的情况远未普及。我们中很少有人能享有离开岗位、小睡半小时的条件。不过，午餐时间和喝咖啡的休息时间是暂时抽身的好机会。面对询问情况的老板，提高的工作效率和警觉性就是你说明午睡合理性所需的证据。

records.title: Take Naps at Work. Apologize to No One [F]

fields.原文: In an ideal world, we'd all solve this problem by unplugging early and getting a good night's sleep. Here's our guide on how to do just that. But the next best thing is stealing away for a quick power nap when you're dragging after lunch.
fields.译文: 在理想情况下，我们都可以通过早点结束工作、放下电子设备并好好睡一晚来解决这个问题。这里有一份教你如何做到这一点的指南。不过，退而求其次的办法，是在午饭后感到疲倦时，抽身去快速小睡一会儿，恢复精力。

records.title: Take Naps at Work. Apologize to No One [G]

fields.原文: In a study published in Nature Neuroscience, researchers tested subjects on their perceptual performance four times throughout the day. Performance deteriorated with each test, but subjects who took a 30-minute nap between tests stopped the deterioration in performance, and those who took a 60-minute nap even reversed it.
fields.译文: 在发表于《自然神经科学》的一项研究中，研究人员一天内对受试者的感知表现进行了四次测试。每次测试中，他们的表现都会下降。但在测试之间小睡30分钟的受试者，表现不再继续下降；小睡60分钟的人，表现甚至有所回升。

records.title: Take Naps at Work. Apologize to No One [H]

fields.原文: “Naps had the same magnitude of benefits as full nights of sleep if they had a quality of nap,” said Sara Mednick, a co-author of the study and associate professor of psychology at the University of California, Riverside.
fields.译文: 该研究的共同作者、加利福尼亚大学河滨分校心理学副教授萨拉·梅德尼克说：“如果午睡质量良好，它所带来的益处与整夜睡眠一样显著。”

records.title: Take Naps at Work. Apologize to No One [I]

fields.原文: Dr. Mednick, a sleep researcher and the author of Take a Nap! Change Your Life, said daytime napping can have many of the benefits of overnight sleep, and different types of naps offer specific benefits.
fields.译文: 睡眠研究者、《小睡一下！改变你的人生》的作者梅德尼克博士说，白天午睡可以带来夜间睡眠的许多益处，而不同类型的午睡各有其特定作用。

records.title: Take Naps at Work. Apologize to No One [J]

fields.原文: For example, Dr. Mednick said a 20-to 60-minute nap might help with memorization and learning specific bits of information. It's just long enough to enter stage-two sleep, or non-rapid eye movement (R.E.M.) sleep.
fields.译文: 例如，梅德尼克博士说，20至60分钟的午睡可能有助于记忆和学习某些具体信息。这段时间刚好足以进入第二阶段睡眠，也就是非快速眼动睡眠。

records.title: Take Naps at Work. Apologize to No One [K]

fields.原文: After 60 minutes, you start getting into R.E.M. sleep, most often associated with that deep, dreaming state we all enjoy at night. R.E.M. sleep can improve creativity, perceptual processing and highly associative thinking, which allows you to make connections between disparate ideas, Dr. Mednick said. Beyond that, your best bet is a 90-minute nap, which will give you a full sleep cycle.
fields.译文: 60分钟后，你开始进入快速眼动睡眠，它通常与我们夜间那种熟悉的、沉浸于梦境的深睡状态联系在一起。梅德尼克博士说，快速眼动睡眠可以改善创造力、感知处理能力和高度联想性的思维，让你能够把不同的想法联系起来。如果还想睡得更久，最佳选择是90分钟的午睡，这能让你经历一个完整的睡眠周期。

records.title: Take Naps at Work. Apologize to No One [L]

fields.原文: Any nap, however, can help with alertness and perception and cut through the general fog that creeps in during the day, experts said.
fields.译文: 不过，专家表示，任何午睡都有助于提高警觉性和感知能力，驱散白天逐渐出现的那种普遍的昏沉感。

records.title: Take Naps at Work. Apologize to No One [M]

fields.原文: So how did we even arrive at this point where aptitude is inextricably tied to working long, concentrated hours? Blame technology, but think broader than smartphones and laptops: the real issue is that tech has enabled us to be available at all times.
fields.译文: 那么，我们究竟是怎样走到今天这一步，把工作能力与长时间、高度集中的工作密不可分地联系起来的？可以归因于技术，但眼光不要只局限于智能手机和笔记本电脑。真正的问题在于，技术使我们能够随时保持在线、随时回应工作。

records.title: Take Naps at Work. Apologize to No One [N]

fields.原文: “We went through a period where people were in denial and business leaders were ignoring it,” Mr. Bersin said. “They were assuming that if we give people more tools, more emails, more Slack, more chatter, and we'll just assume they can figure out how to deal with it all. And I think they've woken up to the fact that this is a big problem, and it is affecting productivity, engagement, health, safety, wellness and all sorts of things.”
fields.译文: 贝尔森先生说：“我们曾经历过一段人们拒绝承认问题、企业领导者也对此视而不见的时期。他们认为，只要给员工更多工具、更多邮件、更多Slack消息、更多交流，就可以假定员工自己能够想办法应付。我想，他们现在已经意识到，这是一个大问题，正在影响工作效率、投入程度、健康、安全、身心状态以及其他各种方面。”

records.title: Take Naps at Work. Apologize to No One [O]

fields.原文: It isn't just office workers who can benefit from an afternoon siesta. A 2015 study published in Current Biology looked at the at the sleeping habits of three hunter-gatherer preindustrial societies in Tanzania, Namibia and Bolivia.
fields.译文: 能够从下午休息中受益的并不只有办公室职员。2015年发表于《当代生物学》的一项研究，考察了坦桑尼亚、纳米比亚和玻利维亚三个前工业化狩猎采集社会人群的睡眠习惯。

records.title: Take Naps at Work. Apologize to No One [P]

fields.原文: “They're active in the morning, then they get in the shade under the trees and have a sort of quiet time, but they're not generally napping,” said Jerome Siegel, professor of psychiatry and biobehavioral sciences, and director of the U.C.L.A. Center for Sleep Research, a co-author of the study. “Then they do some work and go to sleep, and they sleep through the night.”
fields.译文: 该研究的共同作者、加利福尼亚大学洛杉矶分校精神病学与生物行为科学教授、该校睡眠研究中心主任杰罗姆·西格尔说：“他们早晨很活跃，随后到树荫下安静地休息一阵，但一般不会睡午觉。之后他们再做一些事情，然后上床睡觉，一觉睡到天亮。”

records.title: Take Naps at Work. Apologize to No One [Q]

fields.原文: Still, Mr. Siegel said, “the only genuine way to solve daytime sleepiness and fatigue starts the night before with a solid night's sleep.” The real Holy Grail of restfulness is a regular sleep schedule with ideally seven or eight hours of sleep each night, which experts say is optimal.
fields.译文: 不过，西格尔先生说：“真正解决白天困倦和疲劳的唯一办法，要从前一天晚上好好睡一觉开始。”充分休息最理想的状态，是保持规律的作息，每晚最好睡七到八个小时，专家认为这是最佳睡眠时长。

records.title: Take Naps at Work. Apologize to No One [R]

fields.原文: “Daytime napping certainly does increase alertness,” Mr. Siegel said. “But it's not as simple as going to the gas station and filling the tank.”
fields.译文: 西格尔先生说：“白天午睡确实能提高警觉性，但这并不像去加油站把油箱加满那么简单。”

records.title: Take Naps at Work. Apologize to No One [S]

fields.原文: He also advises avoiding caffeine late in the day and waking around the same time every morning, even if you can't get to sleep at the same time every night. This helps acclimate your body to your regular wake-up time, regardless of how much sleep you got the night before.
fields.译文: 他还建议，临近傍晚时避免摄入咖啡因，每天早晨在大致相同的时间起床，即使你无法每晚都在同一时间入睡。无论前一晚睡了多久，这都有助于让身体适应固定的起床时间。

records.title: Take Naps at Work. Apologize to No One [T]

fields.原文: So if you've made it this far and you're interested in giving workday naps a try (or just starting to nod off), here's a quick guide to the perfect nap: Find a quiet, unoccupied space where you won't be disturbed. Try to make your area as dim as possible (or invest in a sleep mask you can keep in the office). Earplugs might help, too. Aim for around 20 minutes. Any longer than that and you're likely to wake up with sleep inertia, which will leave you even groggier than before.
fields.译文: 如果你已经读到了这里，并且想尝试在工作日午睡，或者已经开始打瞌睡了，下面是一份理想午睡的简明指南。找一个安静、无人占用、不会受到打扰的地方。尽量让环境昏暗一些，也可以购买一个放在办公室的眼罩。耳塞可能也有帮助。把午睡时间控制在20分钟左右。睡得再久一些，醒来时就很可能出现睡眠惯性，让你比睡前还昏沉。

fields.原文: I was taking a few weeks’ break from work over the summer. My family and I—my husband and my sons, then 9 and 7—planned to spend the time at our house on the New Jersey shore. When my mother asked what we would be doing on our vacation, I told her we would be together—going to the beach and the nearby amusement park, cooking, playing in the yard. In response, my mother said: “Oh, that’s not much of a vacation for you. I’ll bet you can’t wait to get back to work. Motherhood, it’s the hardest job in the world. All sacrifice!” “Really?” was all I could say in response.
fields.译文: 夏天，我休了几周假，打算和丈夫以及当时九岁、七岁的两个儿子一起，在新泽西海岸的家中度过。母亲问我们假期准备做什么，我说我们会一起去海滩和附近的游乐园、做饭、在院子里玩。母亲却说：“这对你可算不上什么假期。我猜你一定迫不及待地想回去工作。当母亲是世界上最辛苦的工作，全是牺牲！”我只能回答：“真的吗？”

fields.原文: I was looking forward to uninterrupted time with my boys. We would spend days by the ocean and take trips to the boardwalk, where they would scream with delight while riding the roller coaster—the same one I’d ridden when I was their age, then ridden alongside them until Hurricane Sandy deposited it into the Atlantic. We’d ram one another with bumper cars; we’d ride the old-fashioned merry-go-round, waiting until my youngest son’s favorite horse, bright-blue Freddy, became available. Some days were sure to end in tears of exhaustion, but the tears didn’t outweigh the joy. Even on the bad days.
fields.译文: 我盼望着和孩子们不受打扰地相处。我们会在海边玩上好几天，去海滨木板路，在过山车上兴奋尖叫。那也是我小时候坐过、后来陪他们一起坐过的过山车，直到桑迪飓风把它卷入大西洋。我们会开碰碰车互相碰撞，坐老式旋转木马，等着小儿子最喜欢的亮蓝色小马弗雷迪空出来。有些日子难免因疲倦而以眼泪结束，但眼泪抵不过快乐，即便不顺心的日子也是如此。

fields.原文: My mother was only trying to be sympathetic to my life as a working mother, but the self-satisfied way she proclaimed the sacrificial nature of motherhood grated. I don’t believe for one second that motherhood is the hardest job in the world nor that it is all sacrifice. Still, it wasn’t fair to blame her; she was merely parroting a common refrain. Once my annoyance lifted, in its place spread a kind of clarity that helped me to understand how these linguistic tropes reinforce the disempowerment of mothers and women.
fields.译文: 母亲只是想体谅我作为职场母亲的生活，但她以一种自以为是的口气宣扬母职的牺牲性，令我不快。我丝毫不相信当母亲是世界上最辛苦的工作，也不相信它全是牺牲。不过，责怪她并不公平，她只是在重复一种常见论调。怒气消散后，我逐渐明白，这些语言比喻如何强化了母亲和女性缺乏自主权的处境。

fields.原文: The assertion of motherhood as sacrifice comes with a perceived glorification. A woman is expected to sacrifice her time, ambition and sense of self to a higher purpose, one more worthy than her own individual identity. This leaves a vacuum in the place of her value, one that others rush to fill.
fields.译文: 把母职说成牺牲，似乎也是一种赞美。人们期望女性为一个比自身身份更崇高、更值得追求的目标，牺牲时间、抱负和自我意识。这使她自身价值的位置留下空白，而其他人争相填补。

fields.原文: When a woman becomes pregnant, she seems to become public property. Perhaps because bearing children ensures the continuation of the species, it is often prioritized as part of a larger social contract. Not only does this logic lead to an attempt to legislate women’s bodies, but also in smaller, everyday gestures, boundaries get crossed. Many friends tell stories about being touched by strangers during pregnancy, as if a woman’s maternal status turns her into a vessel to handle.
fields.译文: 女性一旦怀孕，仿佛就成了公共财产。也许因为生育能延续人类，它常被作为更广泛社会契约的一部分而优先考虑。这种逻辑不仅导致试图通过立法控制女性身体，也使日常生活中的细小举动越过边界。许多朋友说，怀孕时曾被陌生人触摸，仿佛母亲身份把女性变成了任人摆弄的容器。

fields.原文: Written more than 30 years ago, Margaret Atwood’s The Handmaid’s Tale offers a cautionary tale of womanhood as sacrifice. In this dystopic novel, women are grouped according to the uses men determine for them: namely, sterile wives married for appearance or fertile “handmaids,” who are raped routinely for procreation. One male character declares that the woman must “learn in silence with all subjection” and that “she shall be saved by childbearing.” In this scenario, the act of the concept of motherhood as sacrifice.
fields.译文: 玛格丽特·阿特伍德三十多年前写的《使女的故事》，警示了将女性身份视为牺牲的后果。在这部反乌托邦小说中，女性按男性决定的用途分类：一种是不育、为体面而迎娶的妻子，另一种是有生育能力、为繁殖而经常遭受强奸的“使女”。一名男性角色宣称，女性必须“安静地学习，一味顺服”，并称“她必因生育而得救”。本段最后一句在所提供的纸面原文中语句残缺，无法准确译出。

fields.原文: When we cling to the idea of motherhood as sacrifice, what we really sacrifice is our sense of self, as if it is the price we pay for having children.
fields.译文: 当我们执着于母职就是牺牲的观念时，真正牺牲的是自我意识，仿佛这是生育必须支付的代价。

fields.原文: Motherhood is not a sacrifice, but a privilege—one that many of us choose selfishly. At its most atavistic, procreating ensures that our genes survive into the next generation. You could call this selfishness a biological imperative. On a personal level, when we bring into the world a being that is of us, someone we will protect and love and for whom we will do everything we can to help thrive and flourish, it begets the question, How is this selfless? Selflessness implies that we have no skin in the game. In motherhood, we’re all in.
fields.译文: 母职不是牺牲，而是一种可贵的机会，许多人出于自身意愿选择它。从最原始的生物本能看，繁衍让我们的基因延续到下一代，可以说这种自利是生物本能。在个人层面，我们将一个源自自身的生命带到世上，保护和爱护他，尽一切努力帮助他茁壮成长。这引出一个问题：这怎么能算是无私呢？无私意味着自己并无切身利益，而在母职中，我们全身心投入。

fields.原文: By reframing motherhood as a privilege, we redirect agency back to the mother, empowering her, celebrating her autonomy instead of her sacrifice. Granted, some of us have more autonomy than others. There are many mothers who would not have chosen motherhood, for financial or personal reasons. Still, by owning our roles as mothers and refusing the false accolades of martyrdom, we do more to empower all women.
fields.译文: 将母职重新理解为一种可贵的机会，就能把自主权交还母亲，赋予她力量，赞赏她的自主选择而非牺牲。诚然，有些人的自主权更多。许多母亲出于经济或个人原因，本不会选择成为母亲。即便如此，通过掌握自己的母亲角色，拒绝殉道式牺牲的虚假赞誉，我们能更好地赋予所有女性力量。

fields.原文: In my experience, when women talk among women, our ambivalence or frustration is rarely about our roles as mothers. (That doesn’t mean our kids don’t drive us crazy sometimes.) Rather, conversations turn to questions of how to manage the best part of our lives (those very kids who are driving us crazy) with our partners, careers and other responsibilities. And while many women derive their deepest fulfillment as mothers, it doesn’t preclude their ambition or fly in the face of leaning in or out or sideways.
fields.译文: 依我的经验，女性之间谈话时，矛盾或挫败很少针对母亲角色本身。当然，孩子有时也会让我们抓狂。谈话更多围绕如何协调生活中最美好的部分——那些让我们抓狂的孩子——与伴侣、事业和其他责任。许多女性从母亲身份中获得最深的满足，但这并不排斥她们的抱负，也不与她们选择积极进取、暂时退出或转变方向相冲突。

fields.原文: Calling motherhood “the hardest job in the world” misses the point completely because having and raising children is not a “job.” No one will deny that there is exhaustion, fear and tedium. Raising a family is hard work, but so is every other meaningful aspect of our lives.
fields.译文: 称母职为“世界上最辛苦的工作”完全偏离了重点，因为生育和养育孩子并不是一份雇佣工作。没有人否认其中的疲惫、恐惧和乏味。养家确实辛苦，但生活中其他有意义的事情同样如此。

fields.原文: The language surrounding child rearing as a job surely derived from caregivers’ and homemakers’ efforts to be acknowledged as fulfilling an important role. And clearly raising children is one of the most important things we do—for both women and men—but that does not make it a job. In a job, an employer pays for services an employee agrees to perform. And there is a boss to whom the employee reports. In the case of parenting, who would that be?
fields.译文: 把育儿称作工作，想必源于照护者和家庭主妇希望其重要作用得到承认。显然，养育孩子是女性和男性所做的最重要的事情之一，但这并不会使它成为一份雇佣工作。在工作中，雇主付钱购买雇员同意提供的服务，雇员还要向上司汇报。那么在育儿中，这个上司是谁呢？

fields.原文: That doesn’t mean we don’t want support—paid parental leave, more flexible working hours, publicly funded day care. But the cultural shift has to happen for the policies to follow. Martyrs, after all, don’t need or expect public services.
fields.译文: 这并不意味着我们不需要支持，例如带薪育儿假、更灵活的工时和公共资金支持的托育。但文化观念必须先转变，政策才能跟进。毕竟，被塑造成一味牺牲的“殉道者”，既不需要也不期待公共服务。

fields.原文: Fathers are rarely, if ever, spoken about in the same way that mothers are. It’s culturally acceptable for men to have children and professional identities without having to choose between the two. These unspoken biases run deep. It reminds me of a friend whose husband complained about having to “babysit” the children while she went to dinner with friends. Has a woman ever “babysat” her own children? Things are changing, but the insidious inferences persist.
fields.译文: 父亲极少被用谈论母亲的方式谈论。文化上，男性可以同时拥有孩子和职业身份，无须二选一。这些未明说的偏见根深蒂固。我想起一位朋友，她和朋友外出吃饭时，丈夫抱怨自己不得不“替人看孩子”。女性照顾自己的孩子，曾被这样称呼过吗？事情正在改变，但隐蔽有害的暗示依然存在。

fields.原文: Further, with “women” and “family” as go-to cultural corollaries, studies show, terrifyingly, that these biases are being adopted by artificial intelligence, too. Calling motherhood a woman’s “job” only serves to keep a woman in her place. The priorities of mothers who work outside the home are often questioned. It’s as if women are forced to choose between ambition (or simply earning a living wage) and family.
fields.译文: 更令人担忧的是，研究表明，文化中将“女性”和“家庭”习惯性关联的偏见，也正在被人工智能吸收。把母职称为女性的“工作”，只会让女性被固定在传统位置上。外出工作的母亲，其生活重心经常遭到质疑，仿佛女性必须在抱负——甚至仅仅是挣到维持生活的工资——与家庭之间作出选择。

fields.原文: If we start referring to motherhood as the beautiful, messy privilege that it is, and to tending to our children as the most loving yet selfish thing we do, perhaps we can change the biased language my mother used. Only when we stop talking about motherhood as sacrifice can we start talking about mothers the way that we deserve.
fields.译文: 如果我们开始将母职称为它本来的样子——一种美好而又混乱的可贵体验，将照顾孩子称为我们所做的最有爱、同时也出于自身意愿的事情，也许就能改变母亲使用的偏颇语言。只有停止把母职说成牺牲，我们才能开始以母亲应得的方式谈论她们。

fields.原文: Worried about Internet companies spying on your online browsing? You might turn to something called a virtual private network to protect your privacy. But researchers say these networks can themselves be insecure.
fields.译文: 担心互联网公司窥探你的网上浏览活动？你可能会使用一种叫作虚拟专用网络的工具来保护隐私。但研究人员表示，这些网络本身也可能不安全。

fields.原文: Earlier this year, the federal government rolled back rules that would have prevented Internet service providers from tracking your activity online. Comcast, AT&T and other providers are now allowed to track and sell your personal data too—with much less fear of regulatory action.
fields.译文: 在本文写作当年的早些时候，美国联邦政府撤销了一些本可阻止互联网服务提供商追踪用户在线活动的规定。康卡斯特、AT&T 等服务商因而可以追踪并出售个人数据，而且对监管措施的顾虑大大减少。

fields.原文: One solution is a VPN, which is like a dark, secret tunnel you use to go from your computer to a website. While you’re inside the tunnel—clicking on Instagram photos or checking your bank account—third parties can’t see what you’re doing. There are lots of reasons people around the world use VPNs: to hide location, to access work networks, even to avoid government censorship.
fields.译文: 一种解决办法是使用 VPN。它就像一条从电脑通向网站的隐秘隧道。当你身处隧道之中，点击 Instagram 照片或查看银行账户时，第三方看不到你正在做什么。世界各地的人使用 VPN 的原因很多：隐藏位置、访问工作网络，甚至规避政府审查。

fields.原文: Internet providers handle customer privacy in different ways. Some say you have to opt in for them to sell your data. Because of Internet-connected devices, providers can see more than the websites you browse.
fields.译文: 互联网服务商处理客户隐私的方式各不相同。有些表示，只有用户主动同意，才会出售其数据。由于各种设备联网，服务商所能看到的信息已经不只是用户浏览的网站。

fields.原文: So, who cares whether Time Warner Cable or Verizon knows when I turn off my lights or whether I stock my fridge with Swiss or cheddar?
fields.译文: 那么，时代华纳有线或威瑞森知道我什么时候关灯，或者冰箱里放的是瑞士奶酪还是切达奶酪，又有什么关系呢？

fields.原文: For one thing, those data points can be used to target advertising. And the government or private companies could use the information to deny services, like health insurance—or even water.
fields.译文: 首先，这些数据可以用于定向投放广告。政府或私人公司也可能利用这些信息拒绝提供服务，例如医疗保险，甚至供水。

fields.原文: Some VPNs promise anonymous browsing for free or just a few dollars a month; they claim not to share your data. But these services don’t always deliver on their promises. Sometimes the medicine might be worse than the illness. In the first major review of VPN providers, what researchers found was alarming. Nearly 40 percent injected malware.
fields.译文: 有些 VPN 承诺免费或每月只花几美元就能匿名浏览，并声称不会分享用户数据。但这些服务并不总能兑现承诺，有时解决办法带来的问题反而更严重。在首次针对 VPN 服务商的大规模评估中，研究人员发现了令人担忧的情况：近四成会植入恶意软件。

fields.原文: Experts suggest researching a VPN before using it and to think of it as a supplementary tool, not a privacy solution. They advise reading the VPN service provider’s privacy policy to see whether it collects or retains any user information that could be traced back to you.
fields.译文: 专家建议在使用 VPN 前先进行调查，仅将其视为辅助工具，不能靠它彻底解决隐私问题。专家还建议阅读服务商的隐私政策，查看它是否收集或保留能够追溯到用户本人的信息。

records.title: How Politics Shapes Our View of Evidence [A]

fields.原文: Ask a left-wing Briton what they believe about the safety of nuclear power, and you can guess their answer. Ask a right-wing American about the risks posed by climate change, and you can also make a better guess than if you didn’t know their political affiliation. Issues like these feel like they should be informed by science, not our political tribes, but sadly, that’s not what happens.
fields.译文: 问一位持左翼立场的英国人如何看待核能的安全性，你大致能猜到对方的回答。问一位持右翼立场的美国人如何看待气候变化带来的风险，知道对方的政治归属，也能让你猜得更准。按理说，这类问题上的判断应该以科学为依据，而非取决于我们所属的政治阵营。遗憾的是，实际情况并非如此。

records.title: How Politics Shapes Our View of Evidence [B]

fields.原文: Psychology has long shown that education and intelligence won’t stop your politics from shaping your broader worldview, even if those beliefs do not match the hard evidence. Instead, your ability to weigh up the facts may depend on a less well-recognised trait—curiosity.
fields.译文: 心理学早已表明，即使你的看法与确凿的证据不符，受教育程度和智力也无法阻止政治立场影响你更广泛的世界观。相反，你能否权衡事实，或许取决于一种较少受到关注的特质——好奇心。

records.title: How Politics Shapes Our View of Evidence [C]

fields.原文: There is now a mountain of evidence to show that politics doesn’t just help predict people’s views on some scientific issues; it also affects how they interpret new information. This is why it is a mistake to think that you can somehow “correct” people’s views on an issue by giving them more facts, since study after study has shown that people have a tendency to selectively reject facts that don’t fit with their existing views.
fields.译文: 如今，大量证据表明，政治立场既能帮助预测人们对某些科学问题的看法，也会影响他们如何解读新信息。因此，以为只要多提供一些事实，就能以某种方式“纠正”人们对某个问题的看法，是一种错误。因为一项又一项研究表明，人们往往会有选择地排斥与自己既有观点不符的事实。

records.title: How Politics Shapes Our View of Evidence [D]

fields.原文: But smarter people shouldn’t be susceptible to prejudice swaying their opinions, right? Wrong. Other research shows that people with the most education, highest mathematical abilities, and the strongest tendencies to be reflective about their beliefs are the most likely to resist information which should contradict their prejudices. This undermines the simplistic assumption that prejudices are the result of too much gut instinct and not enough deep thought. Rather, people who have the facility for deeper thought about an issue can use those cognitive powers to justify what they already believe and find reasons to dismiss apparently contrary evidence.
fields.译文: 不过，更聪明的人应该不容易让偏见左右自己的看法，对吧？事实恰恰相反。其他研究表明，受教育程度最高、数学能力最强、最倾向于反思自身信念的人，反而最可能抵制本应推翻其偏见的信息。这动摇了一种过于简单的假设，即偏见源于过分依赖直觉、缺乏深入思考。事实上，善于深入思考问题的人，可以运用这些认知能力为自己早已相信的观点辩护，并找理由排斥那些看似与之相矛盾的证据。

fields.原文: We have to fix the internet. After 40 years, it has begun to corrode, both itself and us. It is still a marvelous and miraculous invention, but now there are bugs in the foundation, bats in the belfry, and trolls in the basement.
fields.译文: 我们得修好互联网。四十年过去了，互联网已经开始侵蚀自身，也在侵蚀我们。它依然是一项了不起的发明，但如今就像一栋房子，地基里有虫子，钟楼里有蝙蝠，地下室里还藏着捣乱的人。

fields.原文: I do not mean this to be one of those technophobic rants insulting the internet for rewiring our brains to give us the nervous attention span of Donald Trump on Twitter or pontificating about how we have to log off and smell the flowers. Those worries about new technologies have existed ever since Plato was concerned that the technology of writing would threaten memorization and oratory. I love the internet and all of its digital offshoots. What I feel sad for is its decline.
fields.译文: 我无意像那些惧怕技术的人一样，长篇大论地骂互联网改变了我们的大脑，让我们像在推特上的唐纳德·特朗普一样，注意力短暂而容易分散。我也无意摆出说教的姿态，劝大家下线去感受生活中的美好。对新技术的担忧由来已久，柏拉图就曾担心书写技术会威胁记忆和演讲的能力。我喜爱互联网以及由它衍生的一切数字事物。我为它的衰落感到惋惜。

fields.原文: There is a bug in its original design that at first seemed like a feature but has gradually, and now rapidly, been exploited by hackers and trolls and malevolent actors: Its packets are encoded with the address of their destination but not of their authentic origin. With a circuit-switched network, you can track or trace back the origins of the information, but that’s not true with the packet-switched design of the internet.
fields.译文: 互联网的原始设计有一处缺陷，起初看起来像是一项功能，却逐渐被黑客、网络喷子和其他心怀恶意的人利用，如今这种利用愈演愈烈。数据包编码中有目的地地址，却没有真实的来源地址。在电路交换网络中，你可以追踪信息的来源，而互联网采用的分组交换设计做不到这一点。

fields.原文: Compounding this was the architecture that Tim Berners-Lee and the inventors of the early browsers created for the World Wide Web. It brilliantly allowed the whole of the earth’s computers to be webbed together and navigated through hyperlinks. But the links were one-way. You knew where the links took you. But if you had a webpage or piece of content, you didn’t exactly know who was linking to you or coming to use your content.
fields.译文: 蒂姆·伯纳斯-李和早期浏览器的发明者为万维网搭建的架构，又加深了这个问题。这一架构巧妙地把全球的计算机连成网络，让人们可以通过超链接浏览。但链接是单向的。你知道点击链接会去哪里，可如果你有网页或发布了内容，就很难确切知道谁链接到了你，或者谁来使用你的内容。

fields.原文: All of that protected the potential for anonymity. You could make comments anonymously. Go to a webpage anonymously. Consume content anonymously. With a little effort, send email anonymously. And if you figured out a way to get into someone’s servers or databases, you could do it anonymously.
fields.译文: 这一切保留了匿名的可能性。你可以匿名发表评论、访问网页、浏览内容。稍费些工夫，也可以匿名发送邮件。如果你找到进入别人服务器或数据库的办法，也可以匿名操作。

fields.原文: For years, the benefits of anonymity on the net outweighed its drawbacks. People felt more free to express themselves, which was especially valuable if they were holding different opinions or hiding a personal secret. This was celebrated in the famous 1993 New Yorker cartoon, “On the Internet, nobody knows you’re a dog.”
fields.译文: 多年来，网络匿名的好处大于弊端。人们觉得表达自己更自由了，尤其是在持有不同意见或想保守个人秘密时。1993 年《纽约客》那幅著名漫画就赞扬了这一点：“在互联网上，没人知道你是一条狗。”

fields.原文: Now the problem is nobody can tell if you’re a troll. Or a hacker. Or a bot. Or a Macedonian teenager publishing a story that the Pope has supported Trump. This has poisoned civil discourse, enabled hacking, permitted cyberbullying, and made email a risk.
fields.译文: 现在的问题是，没人能判断你是不是网络喷子、黑客、机器人，或是一个发帖声称教皇支持特朗普的马其顿青少年。这种情况破坏了文明讨论，助长了黑客活动和网络霸凌，也让电子邮件带来了风险。

fields.原文: The lack of secure identification and authentication inherent in the internet’s genetic code had also prevented easy transactions, obstructed financial inclusion, destroyed the business models of content creators, unleashed the overflow of spam, and forced us to use passwords and two-factor authentication schemes that would have confused Houdini. The trillions being spent and the IQ points of computer science talent being allocated to tackle security issues make it a drag, rather than a spur, to productivity in some sectors.
fields.译文: 互联网先天缺乏安全的身份识别和认证机制，这也使交易变得不便，阻碍了普惠金融，破坏了内容创作者的商业模式，导致垃圾邮件泛滥，还迫使我们使用连逃脱大师胡迪尼都可能被搞糊涂的密码和双因素认证方案。为解决安全问题而投入的巨额资金和计算机人才，使互联网在某些领域拖累了生产力，原本它可以促进生产力。

fields.原文: In Plato’s Republic, we learn the tale of the Ring of Gyges. Put it on, and you’re invisible and anonymous. The question that Plato asks is whether those who put on the ring will be civil and moral. He thinks not. The internet has proven him correct. The web is no longer a place of community, no longer a marketplace. Every day more sites are eliminating comments sections.
fields.译文: 在柏拉图的《理想国》中，我们读到古格斯之戒的故事。戴上戒指，你就能隐身，别人也无从知道你的身份。柏拉图问，戴上戒指的人还会讲文明、守道德吗？他认为不会。互联网印证了他的判断。网络已失去作为社群和市场的功能。每天都有更多网站关掉评论区。

fields.原文: If we could start from scratch, here’s what I think we would do: Create a system that enables content producers to negotiate with aggregators and search engines to get a royalty whenever their content is used, like ASCAP has negotiated for public performances and radio airings of its members’ works. Embed a simple digital wallet and currency for quick and easy small payments for songs, blogs, articles, and whatever other digital content is for sale. Encode emails with an authenticated return or originating address. Enforce critical properties and security at the lowest levels of the system possible, such as in the hardware or in the programming language, instead of leaving it to programmers to incorporate security into every line of code they write. Build chips and machines that update the notion of an internet packet. For those who want, their packets could be encoded or tagged with metadata that describe what they contain and give the rules for how it can be used.
fields.译文: 如果可以从头来过，我认为可以这样做。建立一个系统，让内容创作者同内容聚合平台和搜索引擎谈判，使自己的内容每次被使用时都能获得版税，就像美国作曲家、作家与出版商协会为会员作品的公开演出和电台播放争取报酬一样。嵌入简单的数字钱包和货币，方便人们为歌曲、博客、文章及其他出售的数字内容快速进行小额支付。让电子邮件带有经过认证的回复地址或发件地址。尽可能在系统底层保障关键属性和安全，例如在硬件或编程语言中落实这些要求，让安全性由底层提供，免去程序员在每一行代码里单独处理的负担。开发能够更新互联网数据包设计的芯片和机器。有需要的人可以为自己的数据包编码或添加元数据，说明数据包里有什么，以及其中的内容可按什么规则使用。

fields.原文: Most internet engineers think that these reforms are possible, from Vint Cerf, the original TCP/IP coauthor, to Milo Medin of Google, to Howard Shrobe, the director of cybersecurity at MIT. “We don’t need to live in cyber hell,” Shrobe has argued. Implementing them is less a matter of technology than of cost and social will. Some people, understandably, will resist any reduction of anonymity, which they sometimes label privacy.
fields.译文: 多数互联网工程师认为，这些改革在技术上可行，包括 TCP/IP 的共同设计者文特·瑟夫、谷歌的米洛·梅丁，以及麻省理工学院负责网络安全的霍华德·施罗布。施罗布说过：“我们没必要活在网络地狱里。”实施改革主要取决于成本和社会意愿。有些人会抵制任何对匿名性的削减，这可以理解。他们有时把匿名性称为隐私。

fields.原文: So the best approach, I think, would be to try to create a voluntary system, for those who want to use it, to have verified identification and authentication. People would not be forced to use such a system. If they wanted to communicate and surf anonymously, they could. But those of us who choose, at times, not to be anonymous and not to deal with people who are anonymous should have that right as well. That’s the way it works in the real world.
fields.译文: 因此，我认为最好的办法是建立一套自愿使用的系统，让愿意使用的人能够验证身份。人们可以自行选择。想匿名交流和上网的人仍然可以这么做。有些时候，我们也会选择表明身份，并只与身份可核实的人打交道，这样做也应当是我们的权利。现实世界正是这样运作的。

fields.原文: The benefits would be many. Easy and secure ways to deal with your finances and medical records. Small payment systems that could reward valued content rather than the current incentive to concentrate on clickbait for advertising. Less hacking, spamming, cyberbullying, trolling, and spewing of anonymous hate. And the possibility of a more civil discourse.
fields.译文: 这样做会有许多好处。人们可以更方便、更安全地管理财务和医疗记录。小额支付系统可以让有价值的内容得到回报，改变目前为赚广告费而追逐标题党的激励机制。黑客攻击、垃圾信息、网络霸凌、恶意挑衅和匿名仇恨言论也可能减少，网络讨论有望变得更文明。
